programme: FOSL2 (AP-1/Fra-2) and IRF5 form a macrophage-centered, irritant-inducible inflammatory transcription programme (driving IL6, IL1B, TNF, CXCL8, CCL2, MMP13/TIMP1 and NLRP3-axis genes), and SMARCA4/SWI-SNF chromatin remodeling licenses accessibility at these and other immune loci, coupling the inflammatory output to tissue immune surveillance/therapy response.
role_in_a: In bladder cancer, FOSL2 copy-number state is a prognostic signature, IRF5 marks an interferon-gamma-high, immune-infiltrated molecular subtype with distinct outcome, and SMARCA4/SWI-SNF complex alterations are recurrent driver events whose status predicts response to immunotherapy — together placing AP-1/IRF5 inflammatory signaling and SWI-SNF chromatin state as determinants of the tumor immune microenvironment.
role_in_b: In COPD/emphysema, FOSL2/AP-1 mediates cigarette-smoke-extract-induced cytokine and chemokine gene induction in airway macrophages, and IRF5 drives an NLRP3-inflammasome/Ly6C-monocyte programme implicated in emphysema pathogenesis — i.e. the same macrophage-inflammatory arm of the module, triggered by chronic smoke exposure rather than tumor genetics. SMARCA4's citations on the COPD side concern SMARCA4-deficient thoracic tumors, not COPD's inflammatory pathology itself, so its role in COPD proper is not established from this record.
shared_axis: Cigarette smoke is a shared causal exposure for both tissues — carcinogens concentrated in urine act on urothelium while smoke acts directly on airway macrophages — and in both settings chronic irritant exposure activates the same AP-1(FOSL2)/IRF5 macrophage-inflammatory transcriptional arm, with SWI-SNF (SMARCA4) chromatin state modulating how that inflammatory signal couples to immune surveillance and therapy response in the tumor context.
reasoning: FOSL2, IRF5 and SMARCA4 are independently and specifically documented in bladder cancer, and FOSL2/IRF5 are independently documented in smoke-driven macrophage inflammation/emphysema, so each disease separately anchors the same programme — but no retrieved source states the two diseases share this axis, and SMARCA4's 'COPD-side' evidence is about thoracic tumors rather than COPD inflammation, so the joint claim rests on the reasoner's inference (shared smoking exposure) rather than on retrieved joint-mechanism evidence. The remaining nine factors (ZNF224, HNF4G, HOXB3, SIM2, ZNF335, TRIB3, TRERF1, RFX1, KAT6B) either have no papers, one-sided (bladder-only) evidence, or off-topic hits, so they cannot be added to the carrying set without overreaching.
support: 18358739 shows FOSL2/AP-1 mediates cigarette-smoke-extract-induced cytokine/chemokine gene induction in COPD macrophages; 34041036 places FOSL2 copy-number variation as a bladder cancer prognostic signature; 41639423 shows IRF5 drives an NLRP3/Ly6C-macrophage programme in emphysema pathogenesis; 36582677 places IRF5 in an interferon-gamma-based, immune-characterized bladder cancer subtype; 41438758 shows SWI/SNF (including SMARCA4) alteration status predicts immunotherapy response in bladder cancer; 39817975 and 39513266 place SMARCA4 among recurrent chromatin-regulatory alterations in muscle-invasive and upper-tract urothelial carcinoma.
how_to_falsify: In matched smoker cohorts, compare FOSL2/IRF5 target induction (e.g. IL6, CXCL8, MMP13, NLRP3-pathway genes) and SMARCA4-dependent chromatin accessibility at those loci between smoking-exposed urothelium and smoking-exposed airway macrophages/epithelium (or in vitro cigarette-smoke-extract models of each tissue); if pack-years/smoke exposure does not co-vary with FOSL2/IRF5 target activation in both tissues, or SMARCA4 knockdown fails to alter accessibility at these loci in either tissue, the shared-programme account is falsified.
caveats: Tissue pairing is bladder vs. lung/airway across 325 patient-group comparisons but only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the large comparison count reflects subgroup splits within few underlying cohorts, not broad independent replication. No tissue-generic exclusion list was supplied for this pair (only the single-view list: NACC1, DLX3, BCL11A, OTX1, SOX10, NPAS1, RARG, ZNF165, TADA2A, TAL1, NOTCH1, BCLAF1), so absence of an obvious tissue master-regulator here cannot be attributed to that filter. ZNF224, ZNF335, KAT6B, SIM2 and TRERF1 have no retrieved literature in either disease and HNF4G/HOXB3 evidence is bladder-only, so all six are excluded from the programme rather than silently folded in; per the reader's overall note, joint (cross-disease) mechanistic evidence is missing for every factor, including the three carrying ones.
